statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-96960 (GHSA-7hqp-7c5m-4vq6, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7hqp-7c5m-4vq6): an asymmetric resource consumption (amplification) denial of service in signed-XML processing. Affected: System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 10.0.0 to 10.0.12, fixed in 10.0.13; Microsoft shipped the fix in .NET 10.0.13 (SDK 10.0.113 and 10.0.402): https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/490, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md. The dotnet10-sdk package ships its own copies of System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll under /usr/lib/dotnet/sdk/<version>/ (the SDK root and FSharp directories), which the dotnet CLI, MSBuild, NuGet and F# tools load. Scanned every package built from the dotnet10-sdk source for Alpine 3.24 in the DHI Alpine repository (10.0.204-r0 to 10.0.303-r3, 8 builds; x86_64 and aarch64; including the -dbg, templates and doc subpackages, recursing into zip and NuGet archives) and read the version resources of every copy and the package versions recorded in the SDK's .deps.json files; both architectures match in every build. 10.0.204-r0, 10.0.301-r0, 10.0.302-r0, 10.0.302-r1 and 10.0.303-r0 carry System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 10.0.8 to 10.0.12 (assembly product versions 10.0.8 to 10.0.12), inside the affected range; 10.0.303-r1 and every later build carry 10.0.13 to 10.0.15 (the assemblies in 10.0.303-r1 report product version 10.0.13 although the SDK version is still 10.0.303), which include the fix; the 10.0.13 assembly is also larger than the 10.0.12 one.

CVE-2026-96960 (GHSA-7hqp-7c5m-4vq6): asymmetric resource consumption in System.Security.Cryptography.Xml lets crafted signed or encrypted XML consume excessive resources and deny service. Microsoft fixed it in System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 10.0.13, shipped with .NET 10.0.13; versions 10.0.0 to 10.0.12 are affected (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-7hqp-7c5m-4vq6, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/490). DHI dotnet-sdk-10 for Debian 13 repackages Microsoft's .NET SDK. Unpacked every published dotnet-sdk-10 package in the DHI Debian repository, 10 builds from 10.0.301-0 to the current 10.0.404-1 for amd64 and arm64, including the .nupkg archives inside them, and read the file and product version of every copy of System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll; both architectures agree in every build. Each build carries copies in the ASP.NET Core shared framework (shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App), in the SDK directory and its FSharp directory, and a reference assembly in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref targeting pack, and in each build every copy has the same version: 10.0.9 in 10.0.301-0, 10.0.10 in 10.0.302-0 and 10.0.302-1, 10.0.11 in 10.0.400-1, 10.0.12 in 10.0.401-0 and 10.0.401-1, 10.0.13 in 10.0.402-0, 10.0.14 in 10.0.403-0, and 10.0.15 in 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1. No .nupkg archive in these packages contains it. The dotnet-sdk-10-oci-config packages from the same source hold only a configuration file and a changelog. So 10.0.402-0 is the first build with the fixed assembly, and every earlier build carries an affected version. The range ends at 10.0.402-0.

CVE-2026-96960 (GHSA-7hqp-7c5m-4vq6): signed-XML processing in System.Security.Cryptography.Xml and System.Private.Xml lacked input-depth and operation-count limits, allowed DTD processing by default, did not validate entity references and did not bound encrypted-data candidates or the attributes and namespaces used by C14N transforms, so crafted XML could exhaust CPU and memory (denial of service). Microsoft fixes it in System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 9.0.21 and in the .NET 9.0.21 release (runtime 9.0.21, SDK 9.0.319 and 9.0.122): https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-7hqp-7c5m-4vq6, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/490, https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-96960, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.21/9.0.21.md. We unpacked every published dotnet-sdk-9 package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository, amd64 and arm64, from 9.0.315-0 to the current 9.0.321-1, and read the product version of every System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll and System.Private.Xml.dll (the SDK directory, F#, dotnet-format, dotnet-watch, the ASP.NET Core shared framework and reference pack, and the bundled Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework) in each; in 9.0.318-1 for amd64 we also opened the .zip and .nupkg archives the package carries and found no further copy. The dotnet-sdk-9-oci-config package built from the same source holds only a configuration file and its changelog (checked in 9.0.315-0 and 9.0.321-1). Each copy carries the .NET runtime version of the SDK release it ships with: 9.0.318-1 and every earlier build carry 9.0.20 or older, inside the affected range, while 9.0.319-0 and every later build carry 9.0.21 or newer, which contain the fix. The range ends at 9.0.319-0.
